property_summary: For any fuzzed bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(iid) must return true exactly when iid is the IAccessControl id or the IERC165 id (ERC165 fallback); the mutant drops the super fallback so queries for IERC165's id return false.

For every interface id queried, C.supportsInterface returns true exactly for the IAccessControl id and the IERC165 id (ERC165 fallback); the mutant drops the super fallback, so it returns false when the IERC165 id is queried, breaking the biconditional.

The contract must report support for the IAccessControl interface id (via supportsInterface) for every call; the mutant replaces that check with IERC165's id, so supportsInterface(IAccessControl.interfaceId) returns false, breaking the rule that this selector always returns true.

For any selector, supportsInterface returns true at least for both IAccessControl's and IERC165's interface ids, but the mutant no longer reports support for IAccessControl's id (returning false there while true in the reference).
For any account address, c.hasRole(PROPOSER_ROLE, account) must return false since no proposers were granted in setUp; the mutant returns true unconditionally and violates this for every input.
For any account that is granted a role, hasRole(role, account) must return true; the mutant returns false unconditionally and so breaks this for every granted account.

property_summary: Any account that has been granted the PROPOSER_ROLE by the default admin must be able to successfully schedule an operation; the mutant negates hasRole so the role check reverts for genuinely granted accounts (and role administration itself breaks).

For any arbitrary (role, account) pair that was never granted a role, hasRole must return false (the membership mapping defaults to false); the mutant negates the check, so it returns true for ungranted accounts, violating the rule.

For every role, getRoleAdmin returns the configured adminRole stored in state (TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE for PROPOSER_ROLE/EXECUTOR_ROLE/TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE), which the mutant breaks by returning the role identifier itself.

For any configured role (TIMELOCK/PROPOSER/EXECUTOR), getRoleAdmin must return the stored admin role TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE; the mutant returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE instead, differing whenever TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE != DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (always).
